transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-08-25
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 45 minutes
- Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Ravi Singh (Redwood SE), Monica Park (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (Cyclone), Priya Natarajan (Cyclone), Ethan Cole (Cyclone)

Summary:
Quarterly health check to review usage, cost trends, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment ahead of peak holiday season. Discussed options for Dedicated capacity, KV caching improvements, and a benchmarking plan for late August/early September. Agreed action items and next steps (see metadata).

Topics:
- Usage & cost trends (per-route token counts, embeddings vs generation)
- Reliability incidents and SLO adherence (latency spikes during sale hours)
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs (predictability, cost modeling)
- Roadmap items relevant to Cyclone: per-route throttling, improved telemetry, private deployment options
- Security/compliance checklist for procurement

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're on for 45, so agenda is pretty tight — quick usage review, a couple of reliability items, then roadmap and next steps. Jordan, Priya, Ethan, you good?
[00:08] Jordan Lee: Yep all good, thanks Ava. Quick heads up, we've got a couple of folks out but the three of us can cover.
[00:12] Priya Natarajan: Yeah should be fine.
[00:15] Ravi Singh: Great, I'll start with the usage slide, real quick.
[00:18] Ravi Singh: So for Q2->Q3 we see Cyclone's token consumption up about 42% overall, most of that is from chat routes during promotions, embeddings are steady. The per-route breakdown I sent earlier — generation route for product-recs is the main driver.
[00:31] Priya Natarajan: Right, that makes sense, promo chat gets a lot heavier. Any surprises in cost?
[00:36] Ava Martinez: We ran a quick cost model; effective cost per 1M tokens increased because more long-form context is being sent. Also note you tried a 32k context model for the promotional flows which bumps compute.
[00:48] Jordan Lee: Yeah we did that to improve relevance. But the latency during peak looked shaky on Friday last week — we had several 2s+ tail latencies that impacted the UI.
[00:58] Ravi Singh: I pulled the traces — most of the tail latency came from cold KV cache misses combined with bigger batch sizes at spikes. Your routing policy also funnels everything to hosted in us-east, so you're hitting the same pool.
[01:12] Ethan Cole: We suspected that. Is that something Redwood can help tune remotely, or do we need Dedicated?
[01:18] Ravi Singh: Short answer: both. We can do immediate tuning — increase prefix/KV cache warmers, adjust batching heuristics, and pin critical routes to a higher priority pool. Long-term, Dedicated gives you reserved capacity to flatten those tails. There's tradeoffs.
[01:31] Priya Natarajan: Can you quantify the Dedicated cost vs hosted for our average weekly QPS?
[01:37] Ava Martinez: We'll send a detailed cost breakdown — rough back-of-the-envelope shows Dedicated becomes cost-efficient at sustained high QPS because you avoid burst pricing and get predictable latency. But with current promo spikes, we should model two scenarios: 1) keep hosted and optimize caching + batching, 2) pilot a small Dedicated pool for peak hours.
[01:56] Jordan Lee: That pilot sounds reasonable. We care about both latency SLOs and predictable spend. Also procurement wants checklists — SOC2, SAML, KMS info.
[02:05] Monica Park: On the compliance side, we've got a standard pack — SOC 2 Type II report, ISO paperwork, SAML/SSO docs, and KMS/HSM integration guides. I'll attach those to the follow-up.
[02:16] Ethan Cole: Awesome. Also, can you remind us about data residency and private deployment options? There's a legal ask about keeping some PII in-region.
[02:24] Ava Martinez: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem options and region pinning. For regulated PII we'd recommend Private or Dedicated with encrypted-at-rest keys managed via your KMS. There are some steps for network setup and audit logging.
[02:36] Priya Natarajan: OK. For the short term, what's the fastest win to reduce tail latency before the holiday rush?
[02:42] Ravi Singh: Fastest wins: enable longer-lived KV cache for product-recs, pre-warm cache for promo content, and move the product-recs route into a higher-priority slot to reduce contention. Also reduce max sequence length in the client for promotional flows — shorter context yields big token cost savings.
[02:58] Jordan Lee: Hmm, reducing sequence length could affect quality. How much do we lose?
[03:02] Ravi Singh: It's workload dependent; we suggest an A/B test — keep a control group on 32k, run a sample at 8k with optimized system prompts and see quality delta. We can help run that test.
[03:14] Priya Natarajan: That would be great. What's involved in the A/B? Do we need a pilot Dedicated env?
[03:19] Ava Martinez: Not necessarily. We can do the A/B on hosted using routing rules. If results show a big quality hit, then the Dedicated pilot is next.
[03:27] Ethan Cole: For the Dedicated pilot, what's the typical lead time for capacity provisioning?
[03:31] Ava Martinez: For reserved Dedicated pools we usually need a week or two to provision depending on region and capacity. For an initial small pilot, we can often turn up a preemptible-like pool faster. We'll confirm timelines with infra.
[03:42] Jordan Lee: Okay. On reliability incidents, we had two brief outages in July during the flash sale window. Do you have suggestions to prevent those?
[03:49] Ravi Singh: Yes — we recommend multi-pool routing with automated fallback to lower-cost models, and an autoscale policy tuned to your spike shape. Also increased observability: token-level tracing and long-tail latency alerts. You currently have 1m retention on traces; bumping to 7d for the sale window is helpful.
[04:06] Priya Natarajan: Is increased retention an additional cost?
[04:09] Monica Park: There is a marginal cost for longer retention. We can include the estimate in the cost breakdown. For QBRs we often recommend a short-term retention bump around major events.
[04:19] Jordan Lee: Sounds fine. On roadmap: anything coming that helps per-route throttling and cost controls?
[04:24] Monica Park: Yes — per-route throttling and token-level cost caps are in the Q4 beta. Also a rollout for improved telemetry that exposes per-route latency percentiles and KV cache hit rates. I can share the exact ETA and gating criteria.
[04:37] Priya Natarajan: ETA?
[04:38] Monica Park: We're aiming for early November for the beta; we'll share docs next week.
[04:43] Ethan Cole: Any note on model quantization or cheaper model variants that preserve quality? We were looking at 4-bit quantized variants in a different vendor.
[04:50] Ravi Singh: We have quantized-compatible builds and model recommendations per workload. Sometimes a quantized 4-bit model gives near parity for ranking/embedding tasks but might need evals for chat. We'll propose a recommended model family for product-recs.
[05:03] Jordan Lee: Great. Also another ask — can Redwood produce a short benchmark run against our test traces to show expected p95/p99 tail improvements if we pilot Dedicated + KV tuning?
[05:12] Ava Martinez: Yes, that's part of what we discussed. If you share the traces and preferred SLAs we'll run a benchmark and attach the result.
[05:19] Priya Natarajan: Who owns the benchmark? Is it Redwood or do we need to provision infra?
[05:23] Ravi Singh: Redwood will run the controlled benchmark against our infra; if you want it within your VPC, that's a different engagement. For now we can run it on Redwood staging with your traces.
[05:33] Jordan Lee: OK let's do that. We'll share sample traces by Friday.
[05:36] Priya Natarajan: Procurement will want the legal/ compliance pack. Monica will attach?
[05:39] Monica Park: Yep, I'll attach SOC2, SAML docs, KMS integration guide, and an example SLAs PDF.
[05:46] Ethan Cole: Quick question on single-tenant encryption — can we bring our own keys?
[05:50] Ava Martinez: Yes, we support BYOK via standard KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we offer customer-managed keys in certain regions; I'll confirm region availability.
[06:02] Jordan Lee: Good. Anything on observability improvements we should be aware of?
[06:06] Ravi Singh: Soon we'll release richer traces with KV hit/miss flags, which should help root-cause tail spikes. Also a per-route cost UI for seeing token spend in near-real time.
[06:18] Priya Natarajan: That per-route cost UI will be super helpful for us.
[06:21] Monica Park: We're also working on automated batching suggestions in Redwood Optimize — it can recommend batch sizes based on your request distribution.
[06:31] Jordan Lee: Nice. Back to costs — can you include a modeled scenario where we keep hosted but enable quantized models for embeddings and move some routes to a cheaper model family?
[06:39] Ava Martinez: Yes, scenario modeling is in scope for the cost breakdown. We'll show hosted-optimized and Dedicated-pilot scenarios side-by-side.
[06:46] Priya Natarajan: Perfect. Any blockers on our side?
[06:49] Ethan Cole: We'll need to pull traces and give access to a sandbox dataset for the bench. Also internal procurement will ask for the compliance pack. Nothing else.
[06:58] Ava Martinez: Great. To recap: we'll deliver cost breakdown, schedule an infra deep dive, run benchmark once traces are shared, and Monica will send compliance docs and roadmap slice.
[07:08] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:11] Priya Natarajan: Thank you.
[07:12] Monica Park: Thanks, everyone — I'll follow up with a thread and attach docs.
[07:15] Ravi Singh: I'll set up the infra deep dive and calendar invite.

End of meeting.
